analysis.body:
# AI Use in Construction

According to the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, AI use in construction reached 16.0% of firms in the latest measurement period, up from 14.3% in the prior period. This represents the most direct measure available, collected fortnightly from construction businesses asked whether they used AI in the preceding two weeks. The Census Bureau began tracking this metric in September 2023, establishing an ongoing baseline for the sector's adoption trajectory.

BuiltWorlds, the sector intelligence network serving buildings and infrastructure professionals, identifies AI and machine learning as an increasingly central focus within the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations industry. The organization runs an annual AI/ML Conference dedicated to exploring the landscape of these technologies in AEC/O, examining existing and emerging solutions across all stages of the construction and building operation process. The conference also covers implementation strategies at both project and enterprise levels, supported by case studies showing how companies are deploying specific solutions and lessons learned from their experiences. Separately, BuiltWorlds' annual Buildings Conference explores innovation in building development, design, materials, and systems with particular emphasis on data centers and AI infrastructure.

The Associated General Contractors of America, representing over 27,000 member firms, surveys technology adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders. While the source materials provided do not detail specific AI deployment findings from AGC surveys, the organization serves as the primary adoption data channel for the contractor segment, documenting how firms across the construction workforce are integrating new technologies.

The sourced points indicate that the sector's AI applications span computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning. These use cases suggest deployment concentrated in jobsite operations, preconstruction processes, and safety compliance—areas where computer vision and data integration address persistent industry challenges around labor safety, design coordination, and site monitoring.

Beyond traditional contractor operations, the sector landscape includes venture capital tracking through CREtech and MetaProp, which monitor proptech and contech funding flows alongside broader architecture and engineering technology investment. This indicates that AI deployment in construction attracts capital from technology venture ecosystems as well as sector-specific sources, suggesting ongoing commercialization of new solutions.

Readers considering AI deployment in construction should note that adoption remains below one in five firms, indicating the technology remains in mid-adoption phase. The sector's organized focus through BuiltWorlds conferences and AGC member surveys suggests that implementation pathways and vendor solutions are maturing, but the fortnightly Census measurement and growing adoption rate reflect a field still in active experimentation and scaling.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
